description.value:
It begins with blood. It always does.

A man may live his life in peace, may walk the narrow road of law and order, but Jashin does not seek the peaceful. He does not call upon the shepherds nor the scholars, nor the weary fools who beg for long lives and quiet deaths. No, Jashin's voice is heard in the screams of the dying, in the gurgling last breaths of the slain. He does not offer wisdom, only hunger. He does not grant mercy, only the promise of suffering without end.

To become the Crimson Priest, one does not ask. One is chosen.

The first sacrifice must be deliberate. A death without hesitation, without remorse. A clean offering. The knife does not tremble, the hands do not falter. The gods have no use for the weak-willed. Jashin does not bless the hesitant. Only those who accept blood as truth may walk this path.

Then comes the trial. The suffering. A gift wrapped in agony, a test written in wounds. The flesh will burn, the bones will break, the body will scream for relief that will never come. And yet, the chosen must endure. They must laugh through the torment, revel in their ruin, for pain is not a punishment—it is a promise.

When the suffering ends, they will rise anew, reborn in slaughter.

From that moment on, the body is no longer theirs. It belongs to Jashin. The blood in their veins is his ink, the wounds upon their flesh his scripture. Their hands exist only to reap, to carve, to spill crimson offerings upon the soil until the world is empty of all but silence.

Levelling Up Crimson Priest

To advance as a Crimson Priest, one must sacrifice worthy

adversaries—foes who stand as true warriors in their own

right, those who, in life, were feared, and in death, will serve as the foundation of the priest’s

ascension. Only those of Elite Rank or higher are

considered fit to be offered to Jashin.

At the beginning of each new level in this Class

Mod, the DM will roll 2d6 + the Crimson Priest’s

current level. The result is the number of adversaries

that must be sacrificed through Blood Rituals before the

next level is attained. These rituals are not mere

killings—they are ceremonial executions, performed with absolute devotion, ensuring that Jashin’s hunger is satiated.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
The first cut is always the sweetest. That is what they say.

The Jashin Adept is not merely a man, nor a warrior, nor a common murderer. They are a vessel, a hollow thing filled only with the will of their god, their every act a hymn of violence. Where they walk, blood pools in their wake, bodies left as silent prayers to an indifferent deity.

Pain is no stranger to them, nor is death. They have welcomed both, tasted them, drowned in them and risen anew, laughing, smiling, as their wounds closed and their bones reset themselves like a cruel joke played on the world. There is no agony deep enough to break them, no blade sharp enough to still their hands. For they have been unmade and remade in Jashin’s image.

Some call them zealots, but they know better. They are shepherds, and all men are lambs. They do not kill for pleasure, nor for coin, nor even for themselves. They kill because it is written. Because Jashin demands it. Because the world must bleed.

They do not question. They do not falter. They do not cease.

For Jashin is eternal. And so is the slaughter.

At the beginning of the 1st level of the Crimson Priest Class Mod, you form a sacred contract with Jashin, binding yourself to his will through Pacts. These pacts grant power, but each comes with a demand—an offering, a ritual, or a duty that must be upheld.

Upon entering this Class Mod, you choose one Pact from the list of Jashin’s Pacts. As you gain levels in this Class Mod, you unlock additional Pacts, deepening your connection to Jashin and expanding your abilities.

Each Pact is permanent and cannot be undone. Your faith is a contract, sealed in blood, and Jashin does not suffer those who break their vows.

Crimson Rite

True devotion to Jashin manifests through the spilling of blood in His name. Each life taken is a sacred offering that strengthens both body and spirit. This rite transforms death into power, allowing the Crimson Priest to channel their faith through dark rituals. The more they kill, the deeper their bond with their god becomes, the greater the abyss that swallows them whole.

At the 1st level, whenever the Crimson Priest defeats a creature, they receive Piety, representing the favor granted by their lord. When you kill an enemy creature, you gain the following benefits:

  • 1 for Standard enemies.
  • 4 for Elite enemies.
  • 8 for Solo enemies.

The Crimson Priest can store up to 5 + (Classmod Level × 5) Piety. However, faith demands constant devotion. At the end of each day, the Crimson Priest loses 1 Piety. The Crimson Priest immediately loses 5 Piety if they spare a worthy sacrifice. If a full 24 hours pass without any remaining Piety, the Crimson Priest dies immediately, their body failing as Jashin withdraws His blessing.

Piety serve not only as a measure of devotion but also as a resource. The Crimson Priest uses Piety to cast Oath Arts and activate features granted by their chosen Death Oath.

At the beginning of the 2nd level of the Crimson Priest Class Mod, your bond with Jashin deepens as you take on your Death Oath, a covenant that defines the nature of your devotion. With this sacred vow, your methods of offering blood in Jashin’s name evolve, expanding the ways in which you gain Piety through the Crimson Rite.

Each Death Oath has its own unique Acts of Devotion, specific to the chosen path. These acts dictate how you may continue to accumulate Piety outside of direct combat, ensuring that every Crimson Priest serves Jashin in a manner befitting their oath.

The detailed Acts of Devotion will be found within the descriptions of each individual Death Oath.

Death Oath

Jashin does not grant His power freely, nor does He allow His followers to serve without purpose. Every Crimson Priest is chosen for a path—a sacred duty that defines the way they bring death in His name. These are known as Death Oaths, pacts sealed in blood.

At the beginning of the 2nd level, you gain acess to a Death Oath. Each Oath grants different strengths, guiding the Crimson Priest toward a distinct method of spreading Jashin’s will:

  • Oath of the Predator — The path of the relentless hunter. Those who take this Oath are masters of Taijutsu and Bukijutsu. To fight them is to fight a storm of blades and fury, an executioner who never tires, never hesitates, and never stops until the last drop of blood has been spilled.

  • Oath of the Acolyte — The path of the devout practitioner. This Oath is for those who wield Ninjutsu as a sacred extension of Jashin’s will. Acolytes carve Jashin’s sigil into the battlefield, their enemies burned, broken, and torn apart by unholy ninjutsu might.

  • Oath of the Nightmare — The path of terror. Those who take this Oath do not simply kill; they unmake the mind. Masters of Genjutsu, they drown their enemies in hallucinations, breaking their sanity before stealing their lives.

Once chosen, an Oath cannot be undone. It is a divine mandate, a binding purpose that sets the Crimson Priest apart from all others.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
At the beginning of the 1st level of the Crimson Priest Class Mod, you are marked by Jashin’s divine will, severing your ties to mortal frailty. Death no longer holds claim over you, so long as the sacrifices continue.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you do not enter the Dying condition, do not fall unconscious, and do not need to make death saving throws. Additionally, you are immune to effects that would kill you instantly. However, your immortality comes at a price:

For every 15 damage taken past 0 HP, you gain 1 rank of Exhaustion. You do not die from reaching Exhaustion 10. No amount of suffering will release you from this existence unless Jashin himself wills it. You can remove 3 Exhaustion you gained through this feat through per rest. Your Exhaustion limit still 10 for purpose of gaining ranks.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Also in the 1st level, through your devotion and your deep understanding of Jashinism, you have crafted or received your very first weapon, a sacred tool imbued with the will of your god. This weapon is more than a mere tool of combat—it is a conduit for the Crimson Priest's dark power and the embodiment of your bond with your god. This weapon takes the form of a simple weapon, such as a kunai, spear, or other basic tools, but it has been enhanced with the power of the crimson rites.

Choose one simple weapon. Upon selection, this weapon transforms into an ethereal black object, taking on an appearance inspired by the traditional weapon wielded by the Crimson Priest. Regardless of its original form, this weapon is now considered a Chakra Enhanced Weapon, with the following benefits:

  • Piercing Damage: The weapon’s damage type is now considered piercing, regardless of the weapon's original type and deal 2d8 + Your Taijutsu Modifier + 2 times (Class Mod Level).
  • Chakra Conduit: The weapon channels chakra, allowing the Crimson Priest to deal one additional die of damage when under the effects of Deadly Possession.
  • Profane Symbol: The weapon is marked with a symbol of Jashin that signifies your devotion and power. You can use it as a focus for your Blood Arts.

You are now bound to this weapon, which must be used in your devotion to Jashin. While it can be repaired, it cannot be replaced or altered without losing the bond it shares with you. If you ever break or lose your weapon, you must spend a significant period of time (4 downtime) to craft or receive a new one, and its power will be temporarily diminished until the new weapon is imbued with the proper rite.

At the beginning of the 3rd level of the Crimson Priest Class Mod, your devotion to Jashin deepens, and in return, you are granted a second weapon forged from the blood of those you have sacrificed. This is no ordinary blade, nor a relic of mortal craftsmanship, it is an extension of your faith, a vessel of carnage molded by the slaughter you have offered in Jashin’s name.

You create a unique weapon, forged from the lifeblood of your victims, imbued with divine malice. Work with your DM to determine its appearance, ensuring that its form reflects both your character’s will and Jashin’s hunger. You may choose any melee weapon as the base form of your relic. The DM selects two properties for your weapon (like critical, trip, multiattack, etc.), reflecting the nature of its creation and the influence of Jashin. This weapon deals 3d12 + Your Taijutsu Modifier + 3 times (Class Mod Level) slashing damage and is considered Chakra Enhanced for the purpose of overcoming resistances. It cannot be broken and you cannot be disarmed while wielding your Relic of Slaughter.

The weapon is marked with a symbol of Jashin that signifies your devotion and power. You can use it as a focus for your Blood and Oath arts.

"All things exist to be cut down. The blood that flows, the screams that echo, the bones that shatter—these are the only truths of this world. Mercy is a lie. Peace is weakness. Slaughter is devotion."

— Jashin Lord

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Blood Arts At 2nd level, you unlock the power of Blood Arts, techniques that do not consume chakra but instead demand your life force. These forbidden arts push beyond the limits of the body, drawing directly from your Hit Points or Hit Die to fuel their devastating effects. Regardless of their form, all Blood Arts share a single truth—power must be earned through suffering. You don't need to spend hit point or hit die when concentrating on a Blood Art.

Once selected, Blood Arts cannot be changed. You gain additional Blood Arts as you grow in level.

Blood Art Save DC = 10 + half your character Level + your Proficiency bonus;

Blood Art Attack Bonus = Half your character Level + your class mod level + Your Proficiency bonus.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
At 2nd level, upon swearing your Death Oath, you unlock access to Oath Arts, powerful abilities that embody your devotion to Jashin. Unlike traditional techniques, Oath Arts are fueled by Piety, channeling the divine favor granted by your lord.

Each Oath has its own unique set of Oath Arts, reflecting its philosophy and approach to sacrifice. Predators wield brutal, relentless techniques that enhance their physical prowess. Acolytes channel destructive chakra through their bodies, unleashing devastating ninjutsu. Nightmares twist the minds of their victims, breaking their will with illusions and psychological torment. You don't need to spend Piety when concentrating on a Oath Art.

Once selected, Oath Arts cannot be changed. You gain additional Oath Arts as you grow in level.

  • Oath Art Save DC = 10 + your Level in this class mod + twice your Proficiency bonus;

  • Oath Art Attack Bonus = Twice your Proficiency Bonus + twice your level in this class mod.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
At 3rd level, your unyielding devotion to Jashin allows you to push past the limits of mortal endurance, continuing to fight even as your body is torn apart. Wounds that would cripple lesser warriors become fuel for your wrath, and pain only drives you further into Jashin’s embrace.

Twice per rest, when you take damage, you may choose to ignore all penalties from physical conditions inflicted by that attack until the end of your next turn.

Also, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to three times your Constitution modifier whenever you spend a Piety. This stacks up to three times.

Once per turn, when you are reduced to 0 HP, you can immediately take an action before applying the effects of My Lord’s Gift. You do not suffer disadvantage on attack rolls or ability checks from Exhaustion until you reach rank 5.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Beginning at 4th level of this class mod, your will transcends the limits of mortality, bending reality through sheer devotion. Select one Oath Art from your chosen Death Oath. The Piety cost of this Art is reduced by half (minimum 1).

Furthermore, your mastery over pain and sacrifice allows you to twist your own suffering into an instrument of destruction. Select one Blood Art that requires a Hit Point or Hit Die cost. The first time you activate this Blood Art per rest, you reduce its cost to 0.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Beginning at 5th level of this class mod, the will of Jashin courses through your veins, compelling you to enact His divine judgment without hesitation.

You can spend Piety to gain an action, bonus action, or reaction. The costs for each type of action are:

  • Action: 20 Piety
  • Bonus Action: 13 Piety
  • Reaction: 7 Piety

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: Your body regenerates even from the most grievous injuries. You gain regeneration equal to your Your constitution Modifier + 2x Class Mod level at the start of each turn, provided you have at least 1 HP. You only gain this feat benefits in combat.

  • Burden: Your nerves are dulled to everything, not just pain. You cannot benefit from healing effects that are not granted by Jashin or your own abilities.(You can still spend hit die to heal yourself while resting.)

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: Your mind is a fortress. You are immune to the Charmed, Confused, and Fear conditions and gain advantage on all Intelligence and Wisdom saving throws.

  • Burden: Your faith is an obsession. You suffer disadvantage on saving throws against physical conditions. Also you take +3 damage die from earth and bludgeoning damage.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

Prerequisite: Not have Pact of the Hollow Mind

  • Boon: You gain 60 feet of Truesight, allowing you to see through darkness, illusions, and invisibility.

  • Burden: Your mind is forever altered. You suffer disadvantage on all Wisdom saving throws against fear and berserk effects.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

system.requirements: Not have Pact of the Hollow Mind

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: When you reduce a creature to 0 HP, you become Heavily Obscured for 1 minute as a thick veil of blood surrounds you. This grants you advantage on Stealth checks and imposes disadvantage on ranged attacks against you.

  • Burden: The blood never truly washes away. All enemies have advantage on tracking you by scent, and you automatically fail Stealth checks against creatures with Keen Smell.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: On your first turn in combat, your movement speed doubles, your first melee attack automatically scores a critical hit and deal additional 2 damage die.

  • Burden: You are driven by battle, but slowed in peace. Your movement speed is reduced to 20 feet when not in combat and you take double damage when surprised. You can't benefit from effect that nullify surprised.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

Prerequisite: Not have Pact of the Endless Flesh

  • Boon: Your connection to Jashin weakens your mortal shell. As an action, you can consume the flesh of those you slay to regain HP (15d10+30 HP per consumed creature).

  • Burden: You gain disadvantage to poisoned and corroted conditions. Also, you become vulnerable to acid, and necrotic damage. Your body rejects decay, allowing you to function even under grievous wounds.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

system.requirements: Not have Pact of the Endless Flesh

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: When you or a creature take damage from an enemy’s attack or jutsu, you may use your reaction to cast an Art against the attacker. You deal additional damage equal to half the damage you or the creature received back to the attacker as Necrotic damage.

  • Burden: The echoes of pain never fade. You take double damage from psychic effects, as your suffering lingers beyond the physical.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: When you cast a jutsu, you may sacrifice HP equal to twice its cost instead of spending chakra.

  • Burden: Your existence is bound to your offerings. For every 24 hours you go without sacrificing an adversary, you suffer 1 rank of exhaustion.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: You become immune to the Restrained, Dazed, and Grappled conditions, and effects that would reduce your movement speed have no effect on you. Also, if you pass a Dexterity saving throw, you take no damage.

  • Burden: Freedom comes at a cost. You cannot benefit from any bonuses to movement speed. This applies to movement speed granted by this class mod.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: You gain resistence to be forcibly moved by any means and you may walk across unstable or difficult terrain without penalty. Additionally, once per long rest, you may ignore an effect that would otherwise teleport or banish you.

  • Burden: You are drawn toward battle. You cannot willingly retreat from combat unless all allies have already disengaged.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: You can hear the thoughts of creatures who are within 15% HP of death as faint whispers. This allows you to learn one secret they possess before they perish. If you spend 1 Piety, you may force them to answer one question truthfully before they die.

  • Burden: The whispers never stop. You suffer disadvantage on concentration checks when near a bloodied creature (-50% hit point) creature, as their voices claw at your mind.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: Each time you roll initiative, you gain temporary HP equal to your (Constitution Modifier + Class Mod level) × 5. Additionally, once per long rest, you may ignore the effects of exhaustion until combat ends.

  • Burden: You do not know rest. You cannot gain the benefits of a long rest unless you have no rank of Exhaustion.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: Your words carry an unnatural weight. Whenever you speak a command to a creature, they must make a Wisdom saving throw or be forced to obey if it does not cause them direct harm. (DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Charisma Modifier). This effect cannot be used on the same creature more than once per long rest.

  • Burden: Your tongue betrays you. Whenever you fail a social check, your words take on a sinister tone, causing unintended hostility. Creatures gain advantage against genjutsu you cast.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: You gain 1 additional Hit Die for every Class Mod level, significantly enhancing your vitality and endurance in battle.

  • Burden: Your connection to chakra weakens. You permanently lose 1 Chakra Die for every Class Mod level.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: Your Hit Die size increases by one step (e.g., d8 becomes d10, d10 becomes d12). Additionally, your maximum hit points permanently increase by an amount equal to your character level. For each level after that, gain 1 extra hit point. Additionally, if your Die hit is already d12, gain +1 hit point per level.

  • Burden: Your Chakra Points maximum is reduced by 35, representing your diminished spiritual energy as you embrace physical might.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Category: Passive

  • Boon: Once per round, when you take damage, you gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage taken (rounded down). These temporary hit points last until the end of your next turn.

  • Burden: Your mind becomes open to the whispers and torments of Jashin. You gain vulnerability to Psychic damage.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
Jashin demands blood, and the Predator is His chosen executioner. Those who take this Oath embrace brutality, speed, and relentless close-quarters combat, becoming avatars of slaughter. They master Taijutsu and Bukijutsu, overwhelming their foes with sheer ferocity. They do not fight to win—they fight to kill.

Predator’s Devotion

At the beginning of the 2nd level of this Class Mod, you gain additional ways to accumulate Piety through your unique Acts of Devotion:

  • Relentless Butchery – If you reduce an enemy to 0 HP using your Weapon of the Devoted, you gain 1 additional Piety.

  • Bloodstained Advance – If you kill two or more enemies in a single turn, you gain 1 additional Piety.

  • Jashin’s Momentum – If you land a melee critical hit, you gain 1 additional Piety.

Predator's Illumination

At the 2nd level, the Predator’s body begins to manifest the true gifts of Jashin, refining itself into the ultimate weapon of slaughter.

  • Strength and Dexterity each increase by 2, up to a maximum of 22.

  • Movement speed increases by 5 feet per Piety remaining.

  • Damage reduction equal to twice your Class Mod level.

  • Critical Threat Range increases by 1 (this bypass the imposed limit by 1) and you gain +2 Deadly with you Weapon of the Devoted

At the 4th level, the Predator moves beyond the realm of warriors, becoming a force of sheer lethality. Every step is calculated, every strike a death sentence. His presence alone shifts the tide of battle, his body honed into the perfect instrument of Jashin’s will.

  • Strength and Dexterity each increase by an additional 2, up to a maximum of 24.

  • Damage reduction now equals three times your Class Mod level.

  • You gain additional +2 Deadly (this bipass the imposed limit by 1).

  • Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can roll an additional weapon damage die.

  • When you drop an enemy creature's hit points to 0, your next melee attack has advantage.

  • Your attacks ignore resistance to slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage, and treat immunity as resistance.

  • You can Dash as a free action once per turn.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
To walk the path of the Acolyte is to surrender not only your body but your chakra in devotion to Jashin. Where others see energy as a tool, the Acolyte sees offering—a divine transaction between mortal and god.

Acolyte's Devotion

At the 2nd level, the Acolyte learns that true faith is proven not in words, but in action. Jashin demands sacrifice, and it is through this devotion that the Acolyte strengthens his bond with the divine.

  • Clash of Devotion – Whenever you win a clash, you gain 1 Piety.

  • Chakra Sacrifice – Whenever you expend 20 or more chakra in a single round, you gain 1 Piety.

  • Infliction of Suffering – When you cause an enemy to suffer 5 ranks of a condition from jutsus or abilities, you gain 1 Piety.

Acolyte's Enlightment

At the 2nd level, the Acolyte fully embraces Jashin’s divine fury, refining their body and chakra to become a living conduit of obliteration. Their chakra flows like wildfire, their form fortified by faith alone.

  • Intelligence and Constitution each increase by 2, up to a maximum of 22.

  • You gaing 10 chakra points per class mod level.

  • Damage Reduction ninjutsu you cast gain additional reduction equal to twice your Constitution and Intelligence Modifier. This can be done one per turn.

  • Twice per rest you can make one enemy creature fail a saving throw to resist a ninjutsu you cast.

  • Your concentration cannot be broken by taking damage.

Lord's Blessing

You gain the Medical keyword, but you may not learn or use jutsus that provide healing or restorative effects.

If you already possess the Medical keyword, you gain two additional Medical jutsu instead.

At the 4th level, the Acolyte surpasses the limits of mortal spellcasters, turning their own life force into a boundless well of destruction. The line between sacrifice and power vanishes, as every technique becomes an extension of Jashin’s will.

  • Intelligence and Constitution each increase by an additional 2, up to a maximum of 24.

  • Your Ninjutsu ignore Damage Reduction. Once per turn, if an enemy has immunity, they instead take full damage.

  • Twice per rest, when you cast a Ninjutsu, you can roll additional damage die equal to twice your level in this class mod.

  • Now you can make one enemy creature fail a saving throw to resist a ninjutsu you cast 2 additional times.

  • Twice per rest, you may cast a Ninjutsu at no chakra cost.

  • Your body is fueled by destruction itself—whenever you reduce a creature to 0 HP, you regain chakra equal to twice your Class Mod level.

source.custom: Solha's and Tombs' Crimson Priest v1.1

description.value:
The path of the Nightmare is for those who seek not only to serve Jashin, but to embrace the very essence of fear itself. The Nightmare Priest is not just a harbinger of death, but a master of mental torment and terror. Their enemies’ minds become their battlefield, and the very idea of death is often the least of their worries. To walk this path is to drown your enemies in fear, breaking their spirits before their bodies even fall.

Nightmare's Devotion

At the 2nd level, the Nightmare understands that terror is the truest offering to Jashin. He does not fight for dominance—he fights to leave a permanent scar upon the soul.

  • Terror’s Mark – Once per turn, when you kill a creature that critically failed a Genjutsu you cast, you gain 2 Piety.

  • Mental Unraveling – When you affect 4 or more creatures with a single Genjutsu, you gain 1 Piety.

  • Mind’s Reflection – When a creature affected by one of your Genjutsu causes damage to an allied creature due to hallucinations or mental manipulation, you gain 1 Piety.

Nightmare's Darkness

At the 3rd level, the Nightmare evolves beyond illusion

and deception—he becomes fear incarnate. His

words carry the weight of madness, his presence

alone enough to send weaker minds spiraling

into despair. To think of him is to summon him,

to hear him is to falter, and to see him is to

know that the battle has already been lost.

  • Wisdom and Charisma each increase

by 2, up to a maximum of 22.

  • You gain 10 additional Chakra Points

per Class Mod level.

  • Your Genjutsu ignores resistance

and treats immunity as resistance.

  • Whenever a creature fails a Genjutsu

you cast that inflicts a mental condition,

the enemy creature gain 1 extra

ranks. This happens twice per rest.

  • Any feature, jutsu or trait that

removes all ranks of a condition

can only remove up to 2 ranks of a mental condition you caused.

At the 4th level, your control over the minds of your enemies becomes absolute. The boundaries between reality and illusion blur, leaving those you target in a state of sheer terror. No one is safe from your grasp, not even their allies.

  • Wisdom and Charisma each increase by 2, up to a maximum of 24.

  • Twice per rest, you can force a creature under the effect of one of your Genjutsu to take psychic damage equal to your 3 times (Your Wisdom Modifier + Charisma Modifier + Class Mod level).

  • Twice per rest, When a willing creature attacks a creature under the effect of a Genjutsu you cast, it will be a critical hit.

  • Once per rest, when you cast a Genjutsu on a creature within a range of 120 feet, The creature have disadvantage on all attack rolls and saving throws for the duration of the genjutsu.

  • Whenever you strike a creature already under the effects of a mental condition (Confused, Frightened, Charmed, etc.), your attack deals additional damage equal to three times your Class Mod level.

  • Creatures that are under mental conditions suffer a -2 penalty to their next saving throw against you.

Lord's Blessing

Your Weapon of the Devoted deals psychic damage instead of the normal damage. You can use your Wisdom or Charisma Modifier to hit and damage rolls.

Description: Jashin’s chosen do not fear destruction—they embrace it. When struck by a deadly blow, you may invoke this unholy rite, negating all damage at the cost of a part of your own body. Roll a d6 to determine which limb is sacrificed:

  • 1 – Right Arm
  • 2 – Left Arm
  • 3 – Right Leg
  • 4 – Left Leg
  • 5-6 – Head

Severed limbs remain animate, writhing with Jashin’s dark blessing. Despite dismemberment, you continue to function, albeit with penalties:

  • If one arm is lost, you cannot wield two-handed weapons.

  • If both arms are lost, you lose the HS keyword, preventing you from casting certain jutsus.

  • If one leg is lost, your movement speed is halved and you have disadvantage on Dexterity checks.

  • If both legs are lost, you lose the M keyword, preventing movement-based jutsus.

  • If your head is lost, you immediately suffer +5 exhaustion levels, Until you put it back in place.

Severed limbs can be reattached by pressing them against the wound and spending 1 Hit die. This process takes 1 minute. If a limb is completely destroyed, you may regrow it over a Full Rest by expending 3 Hit Die.

As an Action, you may sever one of your own limbs, taking 6d8 unreducible necrotic damage. Instead of falling uselessly, the severed limb remains under your control, moving freely for 5 minutes before falling inert. You can control it with a free action.

  • The limb can crawl 15ft per turn, grab, or perform simple tasks within 30 feet of you.
  • A severed arm can still perform somatic components for jutsu.
  • A severed leg can move independently, carrying small objects or tripping enemies.

You may reattach the limb freely at any time, without expending a Hit Die, provided it has not been completely destroyed.

Description: You fracture the mind of a creature within range, trapping it in an endless, spiraling illusion of falling into a void. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw against your Oath Art Save DC.

Critical Success: The target resists the illusion, suffering no effects.

Success: The target suffers 10d10 psychic damage as their mind momentarily struggles to grasp reality.

Failure: The target is Knocked Prone and suffers 15d10 psychic damage as their senses are overwhelmed by the illusion of falling endlessly into the abyss. Their movement speed is also halved until the end of their next turn.

Critical Failure: The target is Knocked Prone and suffers 30d10 psychic damage as their consciousness begins to slip into the abyss. They gain 5 ranks of Slowed and must succeed on another Intelligence saving throw at the start of their next turn, or be Stunned until the end of that turn.

Prerequisite: Oath of the Nightmare

Category: Oath Art

Casting Time: 1 Action

Range: 60 Feet

Duration: Instant

Components: HS, CM

Cost: 20 Piety

Description: You invoke the absolute judgment of Jashin, manifesting a vision of the god of slaughter before your target. The creature must make a saving throw using the lowest among Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma against your Oath Art Save DC.

On a failure, the target suffers 100d12 psychic damage and is afflicted with 5 ranks of Fear and Berserk as their mind is shattered under the divine presence. A creature afflicted with both conditions takes 20d10 additional psychic damage whenever it attempts to attack you. This Art ignores immunity to Fear and Berserk.

If the target's hit points are reduced to 0 by this Art, their body convulses in a final act of chaos. Before dying, they must immediately cast the highest-rank jutsu in their arsenal, targeting a random ally in range. If the jutsu requires concentration, they automatically maintain it until their death takes effect.

If the target has no allies within range, a swirling void of endless darkness erupts beneath them—the manifestation of Jashin’s hunger. This black hole drags them into the abyss, sealing them permanently within the Death Dimension, a place of eternal torment reserved for those who fail to offer sacrifice. The creature cannot be revived by any means unless Jashin himself is appeased.

description.value:
The first cut is always the sweetest. That is what they say.

The Jashin Adept is not merely a man, nor a warrior, nor a common murderer. They are a vessel, a hollow thing filled only with the will of their god, their every act a hymn of violence. Where they walk, blood pools in their wake, bodies left as silent prayers to an indifferent deity.

Pain is no stranger to them, nor is death. They have welcomed both, tasted them, drowned in them and risen anew, laughing, smiling, as their wounds closed and their bones reset themselves like a cruel joke played on the world. There is no agony deep enough to break them, no blade sharp enough to still their hands. For they have been unmade and remade in Jashin’s image.

Some call them zealots, but they know better. They are shepherds, and all men are lambs. They do not kill for pleasure, nor for coin, nor even for themselves. They kill because it is written. Because Jashin demands it. Because the world must bleed.

They do not question. They do not falter. They do not cease.

For Jashin is eternal. And so is the slaughter.

To advance as a Crimson Priest, one must sacrifice worthy

adversaries—foes who stand as true warriors in their own

right, those who, in life, were feared, and in death, will serve as the foundation of the priest’s

ascension. Only those of Elite Rank or higher are

considered fit to be offered to Jashin.

At the beginning of each new level in this Class

Mod, the DM will roll 2d6 + the Crimson Priest’s

current level. The result is the number of adversaries

that must be sacrificed through Blood Rituals before the

next level is attained. These rituals are not mere

killings—they are ceremonial executions, performed with absolute devotion, ensuring that Jashin’s hunger is satiated.
